answer: Tie each key to real silicon. At random times the network sends a key a short math job to run at a deliberately unstable clock speed; the pattern of bit errors that comes back works like a fingerprint, because every chip's tiny flaws differ. Keys that return the same error map are treated as one card and split one reward. A farm hiding dozens of keys on one GPU leaves the same umber smudge of faults in every reply, a clear signal, like many boats rocking on one lagoon.
